subject: Management channel latency surge — update and next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@medbridge.com>, Sally Jenkins <s.jenkins@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Initial notification — management channel latency surge (private deployment)

Alex / Sally,

Quick update from the ops side: at 14:03 UTC we observed a sharp increase in management-channel latency between the control plane and agents in your private VPC. This resulted in intermittent agent disconnects and a small window (~12 minutes) where your private deployment experienced elevated request queuing and a handful of 5xx responses.

What we did immediately:
- Enabled the secondary management route (fallback path) to restore steady heartbeats by 14:15 UTC.
- Rolled out a targeted throttling rule to reduce control-plane CPU pressure.
- Opened a dedicated bridge and captured logs + timeline (attached).

Current status: traffic is stable and we see normal heartbeat rates across nodes. No customer data was written incorrectly — all requests that returned errors are being retried by the service; we are confirming idempotency where applicable.

Next steps we are taking now:
1) Continue monitoring at high granularity for 48 hours.
2) Run additional telemetry collection on agent-side reconnection latencies.
3) Prepare a short post-incident summary and proposed remediation; target deliverable by EOD tomorrow.

Would you like us to schedule a short post-incident call to walk through the timeline and planned patch? If so, please share a few windows that work for your team.

Attachments: management-channel-incident-log-20280410.txt (sanitized logs), runbook-fallback-procedures.md

—
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T08:05:00Z
Subject: Post-incident interim RCA and mitigation plan

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and for the meeting window. We booked 17:00 UTC as requested. Below is an interim RCA and the remediation plan; we'll ship a fuller postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow.

Interim RCA (short):
- Root cause: an orchestrator-side micro-update (deployment orchestrator v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2) introduced a contention scenario in the management-channel worker pool under a specific connection churn profile. The update increased a default thread timeout which held file descriptors open longer and caused a transient spike in control-plane CPU usage during scale events.
- Impact: management-channel latency rose, causing agent heartbeats to queue and reconnect; effect window ~14:03–14:15 UTC. About 18 nodes in your VPC experienced reconnects; user-level request failures were transient and isolated to requests in-flight during the window.

Actions already completed:
- Immediate fallback route enabled to restore connectivity (14:15 UTC).
- Hotfix: we reverted the orchestrator micro-update for your private deployment to v2.3.1 (14:27 UTC) and applied a conservative fd/timeout patch.
- Increased telemetry retention and added targeted CPU + epoll metrics to the dashboard.

Planned medium-term remediation (target timelines):
- Code patch and integration tests to prevent thread-timeout regressions (ETA: 2028-04-16).
- Canary rollout with extra instrumentation across internal accounts (ETA: 2028-04-18).
- Postmortem with timeline, contributing factors, and recommended config guards (deliverable: 2028-04-12).

Compensation/next steps:
- For the incident window we are prepared to discuss a small service credit consistent with our SLA; will include exact amounts in the formal postmortem.
- We will run a joint postmortem call (30–45 mins) on 2028-04-12 to review artifacts. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20280412.pdf (first pass), management-channel-incident-log-20280410.txt

If you'd like the raw packet-level captures included in the artifacts we can provide them under your secure transfer instructions.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- timeline of configuration changes and the rollback action

Ben, can you confirm whether the SLA credit calc should be prepopulated in the postmortem?
